_comment: Provisional evaluation dataset for Windows ATT&CK mapping. Review every narrative and expected technique ID before treating these as ground truth. Ambiguous examples are tracked separately and must not be included in binary threshold calibration.

examples.text: PowerShell executes a command encoded in Base64 and launches additional child processes.
A Windows process launches cmd.exe to execute a command interpreted by the Windows command shell.
A scheduled task is created to execute a program automatically at a later time.
A process reads the Windows LSASS process memory to obtain credential material.
A process attempts to access another process memory and modify its execution.
A user account is created on a Windows host and added to the local Administrators group without authorization.
A Windows executable is configured to run automatically when a user logs in by adding a Registry Run key.
A process communicates with an external command-and-control server over HTTP/S to receive instructions and send results.
A process attempts to overwrite raw disk sectors and corrupt the master boot record, preventing the computer from starting.
A process overwrites large portions of a storage device with the intent of making stored data irrecoverable.
Routine scheduled disk defragmentation is performed by the operating system.
An administrator uses PowerShell to retrieve operating system version and hostname information during an approved inventory check.
Windows Update installs approved security patches and restarts the computer during a maintenance window.
An approved backup application reads files and writes backup copies to designated storage.
The operating system performs its regular scheduled storage optimization maintenance.
An IT administrator creates an approved scheduled task to run a software inventory script.
An endpoint security agent scans files and reports detected malware to the management console.
A user launches a browser and opens a company-approved internal web application.
An approved system maintenance tool checks disk health and reads SMART status information.
A software installer creates its documented application directory and adds a standard uninstall entry.
PowerShell executes a Base64-encoded command, but the command content and authorization context are unavailable.
A scheduled task is created by an unknown process, but its command, owner, and purpose are unavailable.
A process accesses LSASS memory, but no evidence establishes whether the access is from a legitimate security product.
An executable is added to a Registry Run key, but its publisher, origin, and approval status are unknown.
A process performs unusually large disk writes, but the target sectors, purpose, and effect on stored data are unknown.
